slot.brief: Two cells with different emfs and internal resistances connected in parallel across an external resistor; find the current through the external resistor (and possibly through each cell) using Kirchhoff's rules.

stem: Two cells of emfs $12$ V and $4$ V, each with internal resistance $2\ \text{Ω}$, are connected in parallel with like terminals together and a $3\ \text{Ω}$ resistor across the combination. Find $(I_R,I_{4\text{V}})$, taking current outward from a cell’s positive terminal as positive.

verdicts.working: Let the terminal voltage be V. KCL gives (12−V)/2 + (4−V)/2 = V/3, so V = 6 V. Thus I_R = 6/3 = 2 A and I_4V = (4−6)/2 = −1 A.

working:
$(12-V)/2+(4-V)/2=V/3\Rightarrow V=6\ \text{V}$.
$I_R=V/3=2\ \text{A}$.
$I_{4\text{V}}=(4-V)/2=-1\ \text{A}$.
$(I_R,I_{4\text{V}})=(2,-1)\ \text{A}$

Independent check: Let the terminal voltage be V. KCL gives (12−V)/2 + (4−V)/2 = V/3, so V = 6 V. Thus I_R = 6/3 = 2 A and I_4V = (4−6)/2 = −1 A.
